column1: Product cost management (PCM) software - evaluation checklist (from the Emithran PCM guide)
Set a weight per row before demos (3 = must-have, 2 = important, 1 = nice to have). Score each vendor 0-3 and record evidence. Weighted = weight x score.

column2: Does it solve our top three problems (e.g. early estimates, quote challenge, target tracking)?
Is the model bottom-up and transparent rather than a black box?
Can we see and edit every assumption (cycle time, rate, yield, overhead)?
Does it cover our main processes well, tested on our part types?
On our 5-10 test parts, is the average difference from known cost acceptable?
Are errors consistent (fixable by calibration) rather than random?
How easily can we calibrate with our own quotes and actuals?
Are sources and update frequency for material prices and rates documented?
Can we load our own rates and supplier-specific data?
Does it cover the regions we source from?
CAD formats, PLM and ERP connections and API access; how much re-keying remains?
Can a designer get a useful number without training, and an expert go deep?
Data hosting, access controls, certifications, export-control and defence requirements?
Licence model, implementation, training, data set-up and support over three years?
Typical rollout, time to first useful result, references like us?
Will the vendor run a scoped pilot on a real programme with agreed success measures?

column1: Average difference (bias: consistent errors can be calibrated)
PILOT SUCCESS MEASURES (agree before the pilot)
Choosing on the demo - always test on your own parts
Buying for one team - involve engineering, purchasing and finance
Ignoring data set-up - a good model with poor rates gives poor answers
Underestimating adoption - a tool nobody uses saves nothing
Expecting one tool to replace judgement - estimates support decisions, they don’t make them
